21.1.intro: Lots of people who see an ad don't click. They tap your name to check you out first. A strong profile makes every ad dollar work harder, for free.

steps.say: Open your Instagram, TikTok and Facebook profiles on your phone like a stranger would (logged out, or in a private window).
steps.check: You see each profile the way an ad viewer does.
steps.lost: Open your Instagram in a private window.

steps.say: Check each profile does three jobs: proves you're real, shows what you sell, and gives a clear next step.
steps.check: You have a list of which job each profile misses.
steps.lost: Is there a clear link to your shop? Yes or no.

steps.say: Fix the biggest gap on each profile with the checklist in Lesson 21.2.
steps.check: Every profile does all three jobs.

21.2.intro: A profile is a mini landing page. The checklist makes sure it builds trust and matches your ads.

steps.say: Go through every row of the lesson's checklist on Instagram.
steps.check: Each Instagram item is ticked or fixed.

steps.say: Do the same checklist on TikTok and Facebook.
steps.check: All three profiles pass.

steps.say: Check the product, offer and look in your current ads also show on each profile (like "free shipping this week").
steps.check: Ads and profiles tell the same story, so trust stays when people tap through.
steps.lost: Put your ad's offer in your bio.

21.4.intro: Posting often enough that you can keep it up beats posting a lot. Batching makes it easy.

steps.say: Pick the posting rhythm in the lesson's table that fits your stage.
steps.check: You have a weekly posting goal for each platform.

steps.say: Batch it: film once a week, then schedule the whole week in Meta Business Suite or a scheduler.
steps.check: A week of posts is scheduled in one sitting.

steps.say: Make every post good enough to be an ad later. Put most of the value in the first quarter of the video. Say key points twice.
steps.check: Your best free posts can become ads, partnership ads or Spark ads. Spark ads are TikTok ads that run a real post.

21.5.intro: Organic reach means people who see your posts without you paying. A few habits grow it.

steps.say: On Instagram, post a trial reel so non-followers see it first. Check results after 24 hours. Share winners with your followers.
steps.check: You test hooks without cluttering your feed.

steps.say: Say your keywords out loud, and put them in on-screen text and captions ("linen shirt for hot weather").
steps.check: Your posts show up in social search.
steps.lost: Put one keyword in your caption.

steps.say: Remake the first three seconds of your best free posts with new hooks (Lesson 19.8). Post them again.
steps.check: Proven posts get a second life.
steps.lost: Give your best post a new opening.

steps.say: Make collab posts with creators and partner brands. Reply to every comment in the first hour.
steps.check: You reach partners' audiences and get early likes and comments.
steps.lost: Reply to every comment in the first hour.

steps.say: Start a broadcast channel or close group for your biggest fans. Answer questions in forums where customers ask for ideas. Say who you are, and never spam.
steps.check: Fans get early access, and new customers find you elsewhere too.

21.6.intro: Reviews, customer posts and kind replies turn curious visitors into buyers.

steps.say: Turn your best reviews into an Instagram highlight, a carousel, and a video where you read them out.
steps.check: Reviews show on your profile.

steps.say: Ask happy customers to tag you. With permission, reshare their posts to Stories and save them to a highlight.
steps.check: Customer posts fill a highlight.

steps.say: Keep shop ratings healthy where you sell through social shops. Reply to bad reviews publicly and kindly, then fix the problem privately.
steps.check: Future customers see a calm, helpful reply.
steps.lost: Reply kindly to one bad review.

21.8.intro: Social shops let people browse your products inside the app. Since 2025, Facebook and Instagram shops send buyers to your website to pay. TikTok Shop keeps checkout in the app, but only in some countries. See Lessons 12.6 and 12.10 too.

steps.say: Connect a clean catalog with one price per product and correct stock.
steps.check: The shop catalog matches your store.
steps.lost: Check your best seller's price matches.

steps.say: Write shipping times and returns clearly in the shop settings.
steps.check: Buyers know what to expect, which protects your shop score.

steps.say: Check which store features don't work in TikTok Shop's in-app checkout (like thank-you page offers). Check seller fees. Make sure in-app orders flow into your store and email app.
steps.check: In-app orders make money and land in your normal systems.

21.9.intro: A profile that's out of date or doesn't match your ads loses buyers. Helix doesn't check your social profiles yet, so this is your own 10-minute check.

steps.say: Read the checks in the lesson's table.
steps.check: You know what to look at.

steps.say: Open your Instagram profile. Mark each row pass or fail.
steps.check: You have a short list of rows that fail.
steps.lost: Mark one row pass or fail.

steps.say: Fix one failed item this week.
steps.check: One less row fails when you check again next month.
